plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in Sydney turn lavender-purple as this tree comes into full bloom. Clouds of trumpet-shaped flowers cover the fern-like canopy. They drop to carpet the pavement in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November, peaking in November in Sydney)
plants.location: Sydney, Australia, and other warm-temperate cities of the Southern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Jacarandas flower so reliably in Sydney in late spring that the University of Sydney's famous jacaranda became a symbol of exam season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: While most garden shrubs are shutting down for winter, this glossy evergreen opens fragrant, silky blossoms, from single saucer shapes to ruffled peony forms. They brighten the autumn garden with pinks and whites.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter (October to November, often continuing through December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan and widely grown in temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Sasanqua camellias are close relatives of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In its native Mexico, the poinsettia grows as a leggy shrub. Its blazing red leaf-like bracts surround tiny yellow true flowers as the short days of late autumn arrive.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to December)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America, now grown in warm climates worldwide
plants.funFact: The vivid red parts people take for petals are actually modified leaves called bracts. The real flowers are the small yellow clusters at their centre.
